Have you ever zoned out on a Zoom call, then realised you’ve missed the last two minutes? I’ve been trying Wispr Flow’s Notetaker, which records and transcribes meetings in real time. You can ask it what you missed, search previous meetings for specific decisions, and use the transcripts with tools like ChatGPT and Claude to draft follow-up emails or messages. Very useful if, like me, you spend a lot of time in meetings, and even more time trying to remember what actually happened in them.  It’s currently available on Mac and Windows, and the Notetaker is free to use. Copy the link for one month of Wispr Flow Pro for free: https://ref.wisprflow.ai/ali_tiktok_notetaker

For decades, cardiology treated a woman's heart like a smaller version of a man's, and the hormonal transitions she lives through were a footnote. Today the American Heart Association, the American Academy of Pediatrics, ACOG, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine released a joint framework. It puts perimenopause and postmenopause on the same map as your first period and your reproductive years, and it treats every one of those stages as a cardiovascular checkpoint, with its own screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. Menopause weight gain isn’t a willpower problem. Your scale can barely move while your body changes underneath it: more fat around your organs, less muscle, and an appetite system working against you. A review published in September in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences pulls together 25 years of research on what falling estrogen does to appetite. Estrogen helps run the hunger switch in the hypothalamus; when it falls, the balance tips toward hunger. Leptin, the hormone that tells your brain you’ve had enough, rises, but the brain responds to it less. Ghrelin, your hunger hormone, dips after a meal but climbs back faster.
